## Type notation and inspection {#conventions}

Topic types use `package/msg/TypeName`; service types use `package/srv/TypeName`. Inside `.msg` files, `geometry_msgs/Point` refers to `geometry_msgs/msg/Point`, and `EngineCommand` refers to `pylon_interfaces/msg/EngineCommand` in the same package.

`float64[9]` is a fixed array of nine elements; `EngineCommand[<=16]` is a variable array of at most 16 elements; `string[]` is an unbounded variable array. A `—` in the value column means no explicit default. ROS 2 implicit defaults are zero for numbers, false for bool, an empty string for string, and an empty array for variable arrays. Constants are listed separately from fields. Consult source comments and API pages for units, frames, and validity conditions; a field type alone does not define units.

After sourcing ROS and the PyLoN workspace, inspect the installed types with:

```bash
ros2 interface list
ros2 topic type /ksp_vessel/ground_truth/flight
ros2 interface show pylon_interfaces/msg/FlightState
ros2 interface show pylon_interfaces/srv/GetSeparationResult
```

Notation follows the [ROS 2 interface definition specification](https://design.ros2.org/articles/legacy_interface_definition.html).
